statements.statement: The expression 0 == "" evaluates to true in JavaScript/TypeScript.
statements.explanation: Double equals (==) performs type coercion, so 0 == "" is true. This is why you should always use triple equals (===).

statements.statement: The operator === checks equality after converting both values to the same type.
statements.explanation: Triple equals (===) does NOT convert types. If the types don't match, it simply returns false. Double equals (==) is the one that converts types.
Both values are the same type (number) and the same value (25), so === returns true.
